axes.local_files:
The IDE/plugin/CLI forms work with your local code and projects (official security page: Qoder CN can handle local code, installed extensions,
remote connections and external services); the CLI's memory files (AGENTS.md and automatic memory) are stored on your machine, viewable and clearable in settings.
Model inference happens server-side — the series page's official line: "the full chain is deployed on domestic cloud";
the data boundaries of the Cloud Agents CN / QoderWake CN lines were not verified item by item.
axes.background:
The background/async surface is part of the official narrative: Cloud Agents CN runs fully managed long-running async tasks (official wording: tasks keep running after the client closes
(translated)),
batch concurrent execution; the CLI has scheduled tasks, /loop repeated execution, Cloud Mode and Remote Control;
the mobile app can view agent progress and approve key operations (official-site framing).
Note the official notice "Qoder CN IDE 'Quest' panel retirement notice" — the Quest surface in old tutorials is outdated.
axes.fit:
Fits: the domestic compliance narrative (a first-party Alibaba Cloud product, mainstream domestic LLMs + domestic cloud deployment, finance/government customers named officially),
IDE/JetBrains-plugin/CLI trio under one account, family-wide shared Credits, enterprise VPC dedicated deployment.
Does not fit: those wanting a self-selectable overseas model list (the mainline model surface is domestic mainstream LLMs), or still relying on the VS Code plugin (no longer maintained).
axes.name_history:
The brand renaming history (dossiers must state it clearly): the intelligent coding assistant Tongyi Lingma (Lingma, first launched 2023) → the Qoder CN series
(officially renamed 2026-05-20); the desktop app was formerly named Lingma IDE, Qoder CN Desktop —
the same product under multiple names across periods; when searching, recognize Tongyi Lingma / Lingma / Qoder CN alike.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs.

The test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md).

**Suggested measurement** (three items, all pointing at what the official readable pages do not provide):

- **the actual feature differences between the international qoder.com and the domestic qoder.com.cn** (no official comparison table)
- **the migration path for existing workflows after the Quest panel retirement** (the notice only says retired, no item-by-item migration guide)
- **the CLI non-interactive mode's actual permission-approval behavior in CI/CD** (how the approval flow blocks in headless mode)
unknowns:
- Where each underlying model's filing number is publicly disclosed (the official docs claim domestic-deployment compliance; filing numbers not verified item by item)
- The product relationship between the international qoder.com and the CN series (no official cross-reference page)
- Storage and retention policies of the Cloud Agents CN / QoderWake CN lines (not verified item by item)
- Console details of the Enterprise Standard/Dedicated (VPC) editions (not verified item by item)
related: both are domestic big-tech coding assistants: Tencent's Hunyuan-backed CodeBuddy has a verifiable filing and rides its cloud ecosystem end to end; Qoder CN runs the "first-party product + family Credits" narrative, and this site has not verified its filing number

both are domestic coding tools with overseas lines: ByteDance's Trae is active on both domestic and international lines; the official relationship between Qoder CN's domestic line (qoder.com.cn) and international edition (qoder.com) has no official cross-reference

same brand, two lines: the international line uses qoder.com accounts and overseas endpoints, its family includes Cloud Agents/QoderWork; do not infer features or model surfaces across the lines (no official comparison page)
